newsitem.title: USA: Amex has higher earnings, announces major job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Amex has higher earnings, announces major job cuts.

text.p: American Express Co., reporting higher-than-expected fourth quarter earnings, said Monday it would cut 3,300 jobs from a worldwide work force of about 60,000 as part of a continuing reorganization of its Travel Related Services unit.
About 2,000 of the job cuts will be made overseas and some facilities will be consolidated, American Express said.

Spokeswoman Susan Miller said some of the employees who will be affected by the restructuring have been alerted but for others details were still being worked out. She said the 3,300 figure represented both job eliminations and the number of people being let go.
Regarding the facilities to be consolidated, she said "they are not the major locations."
American Express, the travel, financial and network services provider, had fourth quarter earnings of $595 million, or $1.23 a share.
A consensus of earnings estimates by First Call Inc. called for American Express to earn 89 cents a share.
A year earlier it earned $384 million, or 77 cents a share.
